title: Remarks at Valley City, N.D
paragraphs: In greeting you all, let me first say a special word of greeting to the veterans of the great war, to the men without whom we would not have any country here of which to be proud; and next to my own comrades, the men of the National Guard, the men some of whom served in the Philippine Islands. All that I can say of ourselves, the men of the lesser war, is that we tried to follow in the footsteps of the men of the great war.

I greet you all. I feel at home here in North Dakota. It was twenty-three years ago that I first came to your state, when it was then a territory. I know you well. I congratulate you upon upon all you do in wheat growing and stock raising, but above all, in the kind of men and women you grow. (Applause) And here, with your normal and your high schools, whose professor I have just met, I see you are preparing for the next crop -- the children. (Applause)
